title: [Security High] Add security headers to sync server
description:
Sync server is missing essential security headers.

## File
- server/src/main.rs

## Missing Headers
- `X-Frame-Options: DENY` - Clickjacking protection
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` - MIME sniffing protection
- `Strict-Transport-Security` - HSTS
- `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` - Prevent referrer leakage
- `Content-Security-Policy` - Server-side CSP

## Fix Required
```rust
use tower_http::set_header::SetResponseHeaderLayer;
use http::header;

// Add to middleware stack
.layer(SetResponseHeaderLayer::if_not_present(
    header::X_FRAME_OPTIONS,
    HeaderValue::from_static("DENY"),
))
.layer(SetResponseHeaderLayer::if_not_present(
    header::X_CONTENT_TYPE_OPTIONS,
    HeaderValue::from_static("nosniff"),
))
```

## Priority
HIGH - Missing standard security protections

[Security High] Strengthen password requirements
description:
Password validation only enforces minimum length, allowing weak passwords.

## Files
- server/src/api/auth.rs (line 35)
- server/src/api/user.rs (line 334)

## Current
- Minimum 12 characters
- No complexity requirements

## Issue
Passwords like 'aaaaaaaaaaaa' or '123456789012' are accepted.

## Fix Required
Add complexity requirements:
1. At least one uppercase letter
2. At least one lowercase letter
3. At least one number
4. At least one special character

Or use password strength estimation (zxcvbn crate).

```rust
fn validate_password_strength(password: &str) -> Result<(), PasswordError> {
    if password.len() < 12 { return Err("Too short"); }
    if !password.chars().any(|c| c.is_uppercase()) { return Err("Need uppercase"); }
    // etc.
}
```

## Priority
HIGH - Weak passwords accepted

title: Auto-detect language from browser with settings override
description:
Use the browser's Accept-Language header for automatic language detection, with the ability to override in settings.

## Current behaviour
- Language must be manually selected in settings
- No automatic detection

## Proposed behaviour
- Default to 'Auto' which uses browser language preference
- Match browser language to available locales
- Fall back to en-GB if no match
- Allow override in settings dropdown
- First option in dropdown: 'Auto (detected: XX)'

## Implementation
1. Read `navigator.language` or `navigator.languages`
2. Match against available locale files
3. Store preference as 'auto' or specific locale code
4. When 'auto', resolve at runtime

## Settings UI
- Language dropdown options:
  - Auto (detected: English) <- shows detected language
  - English (UK)
  - English (US)
  - German
  - etc.

## Consistency
- Match pattern of other 'Auto' options (theme, mobile/desktop view)

## Fallback chain
1. User-selected override
2. Browser primary language
3. Browser secondary languages
4. en-GB (default)

- Hard-coded colour names
- Status/state comparisons using raw strings

- `status === 'active'`
- Raw string comparisons without constants

title: [Security High] TUI: Fix temporary plaintext API key storage
description:
API keys are stored with 'PLAINTEXT:' prefix temporarily after device registration.

## File
- tui/src/ui/operations/settings.rs (line 293)

## Code
```rust
metadata.api_key = Some(format!("PLAINTEXT:{}", creds.api_key));
```

## Issue
- API keys exist in unencrypted form in SQLite database
- Vulnerable window: Between device registration and next app lock/unlock
- If database accessed during this window, API keys are compromised

## Fix Required
- Encrypt API key immediately on registration using session key
- Or require immediate app lock/unlock after registration
- Remove PLAINTEXT: prefix pattern entirely

## Priority
HIGH - Credential exposure in database

title: [Security Medium] TUI: Set restrictive file permissions on remember file
description:
The .jottery_remember file is created with default permissions.

## File
- tui/src/ui/operations/auth.rs (line 214)

## Current Code
```rust
std::fs::write(&remember_file, &encrypted_json)
```

## Issue
- Uses OS default permissions (typically 644 on Unix)
- File may be world-readable
- Contains obfuscated password (see hardcoded device key issue)

## Fix Required
Set restrictive permissions (mode 0600):
```rust
use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt;

let mut file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
    .write(true)
    .create(true)
    .truncate(true)
    .mode(0o600)  // Owner read/write only
    .open(&remember_file)?;
file.write_all(&encrypted_json)?;
```

## Priority
MEDIUM - Reduces exposure of obfuscated password

100,000 iterations for master key derivation.

## OWASP Recommendation (2023)
600,000+ iterations for PBKDF2-SHA256

## Note
- SQLCipher already uses 256,000 (tui/src/db.rs line 36)
- Higher iterations = longer unlock time

## Considerations
- UX impact: Each doubling roughly doubles unlock time
- Migration: Need to re-encrypt with new params on password change
- Test performance on target hardware

## Fix Required
1. Increase to 256,000+ iterations
2. Implement migration strategy for existing databases
3. Consider migrating to Argon2id (mentioned in CLAUDE.md)

## Priority
MEDIUM - Improves brute-force resistance

title: [Security Medium] Server: Log JSON parsing errors instead of silent defaults
description:
JSON parsing failures silently default to empty data.

## File
- server/src/api/sync.rs (lines 287-288, 656, 735, 738)

## Current Code
```rust
let server_tags: Vec<String> = serde_json::from_str(&server_note.tags)
    .unwrap_or_default();
```

## Issue
If tags JSON is corrupted:
- Silently becomes empty array
- No error logged for investigation
- Data loss goes unnoticed

## Fix Required
Log when defaults are used:
```rust
let server_tags: Vec<String> = serde_json::from_str(&server_note.tags)
    .inspect_err(|e| tracing::warn!("Failed to parse tags for note {}: {}", note_id, e))
    .unwrap_or_default();
```

Or return error to client:
```rust
let server_tags: Vec<String> = serde_json::from_str(&server_note.tags)
    .map_err(|e| AppError::InternalError(format!("Corrupted tags: {}", e)))?;
```

## Priority
MEDIUM - Silent data corruption

title: [Security Critical] Implement rate limiting on auth endpoints
description:
Sync server has zero rate limiting on authentication endpoints.

## Affected File
- server/src/main.rs (lines 156-159)

## Unprotected Endpoints
- POST /api/v1/auth/register-user
- POST /api/v1/auth/register-device
- POST /api/v1/auth/login
- POST /api/v1/user/login

## Attack Vectors
1. **Password brute forcing** - Unlimited login attempts
2. **Account enumeration** - Different timing for valid/invalid emails
3. **Registration spam** - Unlimited account creation
4. **Device flood** - Unlimited device registrations

## Note
- tower_governor dependency exists in Cargo.toml (line 48-49) but is NOT USED

## Fix Required
```rust
use tower_governor::{governor::GovernorConfig, GovernorLayer};

// 5 requests per second per IP
let config = GovernorConfig::default();
let governor = GovernorLayer::new(&config);

// Apply to auth routes
.route("/api/v1/auth/login", post(login))
.layer(governor)
```

## Priority
CRITICAL - Enables brute force attacks

title: [Security High] TUI: Document/warn about hardcoded device key
description:
Hardcoded constant used as encryption key for 'Remember Password' feature.

## Files
- tui/src/ui/operations/auth.rs (lines 168-171)
- tui/src/main.rs (lines 232-234)

## Code
```rust
let constant = b"jottery-tui-device-key-v1.0.0---";
let mut key = [0u8; 32];
key.copy_from_slice(&constant[..32]);
```

## Existing Warning in Code
Line 167: "WARNING: This is not cryptographically secure, just obfuscation"

## Issue
- Anyone with source code can decrypt stored passwords
- This is obfuscation, not encryption
- Currently documented in code but not in UI/docs

## Fix Options
1. **Minimum**: Add prominent UI warning when enabling 'Remember Password'
2. **Better**: Use OS keychain (macOS Keychain, Linux secret-service, Windows Credential Manager)
3. **Alternative**: Use machine-specific key derivation (hardware ID + salt)

## Priority
HIGH - Security expectation mismatch

[Security Medium] TUI: Implement memory zeroization for sensitive data
description:
Sensitive data (keys, passwords) not properly zeroized in memory.

## Files
- tui/src/crypto/key_manager.rs (line 78): Key cloning without zeroization
- tui/src/ui/operations/auth.rs (line 142): Password string cloned

## Issues
1. **MasterKey cloning** - Creates multiple copies in memory
   - Line 78: `master_key.clone()`
   - MasterKey struct doesn't implement Zeroize trait
   
2. **Password strings** - Not zeroized on drop
   - Line 142: `app.password_input.clone()`
   - Standard String doesn't zeroize on drop
   - Line 152: Only clears one instance

3. **Debug logging** - Key bytes logged
   - Line 46-47: First 8 bytes of key logged in debug mode

## Fix Required
1. Add `zeroize` crate dependency
2. Implement `Zeroize` trait for MasterKey
3. Use `Zeroizing<String>` for password handling
4. Remove sensitive data from debug logs

```rust
use zeroize::{Zeroize, Zeroizing};

struct MasterKey {
    key: Zeroizing<[u8; 32]>,
}
```

## Priority
MEDIUM - Reduces memory attack surface

title: [Security Medium] Enforce HTTPS for sync endpoints
description:
HTTP endpoints are allowed for sync server connections.

## Files
- src/lib/components/settings/SyncSetupForm.svelte: No protocol enforcement
- tui/src/models/settings.rs (line 281): Accepts both http:// and https://

Users can configure http:// sync endpoints, transmitting:

- API keys
- Encrypted note data

1. **Web client**: Validate endpoint starts with https://
   - Allow http://localhost and http://127.0.0.1 for development
   
2. **TUI client**: Same validation
   - Add warning if http:// used in production

title: TUI: Sync attachments between clients
description:
CRITICAL BUG: The TUI sync implementation does not sync attachments.

Current behavior:
- Line 1950 in src/ui/app.rs: `attachments: vec![], // TODO: Handle attachments`
- When syncing notes, attachments are stripped out and replaced with empty array
- Attachments added in web client don't appear in TUI
- Attachments added in TUI don't appear in web client

What needs to be done:
1. When PUSHING notes to server:
   - Include attachments array in SyncNote
   - Attachments are already encrypted in the database
   - Need to read from attachments table and include in sync payload

2. When PULLING notes from server:
   - Process attachments array from server response
   - Store attachments in local attachments table
   - Update note.attachments array

3. Handle attachment conflicts:
   - If same attachment ID exists, compare hashes
   - If different, keep newer version or both (append ID suffix)

4. Test bidirectional sync with attachments

Without this, attachments are client-local only and sync is broken for any notes with attachments.
